evidence.s1_ci: ci.yml runs on pull_request and push to main, runs `npm ci`, `npm test`, `npm run build` in site/ (all real scripts in site/package.json: test, pretest→prepare-data, build with svelte-check). It has `permissions: contents: read`, no secrets, a comment warning against pull_request_target, and a PR-title check that passes the title through env (no injection). pages.yml triggers on push to main plus workflow_dispatch (no branch guard on manual runs). Its top-level permission is contents: read, and only the deploy job has pages/id-token write. Weaknesses: none of the actions are pinned to commit SHAs (actions/checkout@v4, setup-node@v4, configure-pages@v5, upload-pages-artifact@v3, deploy-pages@v4 in ci.yml:90-92, pages.yml:169-210, release.yml:247-251). release.yml:233-234 grants `contents: write` to the whole job, which also runs `npm ci`/test/build, so the permissions are not least-privilege. Nothing was run or published.
evidence.s1_readme: README (step1.patch 508-625) covers install (Node 22 via .nvmrc, `cd site && npm ci`), develop (`npm run dev`), test (`npm test`), build (`npm run build`, `npm run preview`, PAGES_BASE, which vite.config.ts:11 reads), a script table (prepare-data, index, fieldsets, sample-bullets all exist in site/package.json), data contribution (families, sources, sample_* generated, issue forms that exist in .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE) and license (MIT LICENSE, THIRD-PARTY.md exist). The claim that generated files are not committed matches site/.gitignore.
evidence.s1_release: There is one strategy. The version lives in site/package.json (0.1.0) and its lock file, under SemVer with pre-1.0 rules. A release is made with a tag-triggered release.yml that checks the tag is on main, matches package.json and package-lock.json, and has a CHANGELOG section, then publishes the notes and assets. CONTRIBUTING.md gives a step-by-step release checklist (`npm version X.Y.Z --no-git-tag-version`, `chore(release): X.Y.Z`). CHANGELOG.md states Keep a Changelog 1.1.0 and has an Unreleased section. Dependabot updates npm (/site) and github-actions weekly, grouped, with chore/ci prefixes that match the convention. The convention (Conventional Commits plus a `data` type) is stated in CONTRIBUTING and the README. All 7 commits in commits.txt follow it (ci:, docs:, feat(site):, fix(site):).
evidence.s2_requirements: Route: router.ts parses `#/compare/<a>/<b>` with decoding and a fallback, and App.svelte lazy-loads Compare.svelte. The hash route survives a reload. SVG: Compare.svelte draws one <path> per outline from overlayProfiles (caseOuterProfile, one viewport, head at z=0), with role=img and aria-label `Profiles of {a} and {b}` using record names. Table: the <caption> reads `Dimensions (mm|in)` and the headers are Symbol / name A / name B / Difference. Rows come only from the `cartridge` part, skip Tol fields and FIELD_UNITS entries, label symbols with FIELD_LABELS, and compute Difference as B−A. Units follow unitSystem() (the Default units setting): formatValue for metric, displayNumber for inches. Cartridge.svelte adds a labelled `Compare with` NativeSelect of the other entries sorted by name and a `Compare` button that sets href.compare(key, chosen). German strings were added in i18n.svelte.ts. Shot cartridges are refused by overlayProfiles.
evidence.s2_correctness: I checked the test values against the data: 308 Win. L3 51.18 / 300 Win. Mag. L3 66.55 gives 15.37, e min 1.4/0.94 gives -0.46, and the imperial values come from displayNumber(…,'in') with no extra rounding. The difference is computed in mm and then converted, which is correct. The head faces align because viewportFor uses a shared zMin and both profiles start at z=0 (the test checks equal min x and a common axis). The scale check (66.55−51.18)·4 holds. Floating-point noise in metric differences is removed with displayNumber(…,'mm') (toPrecision(12)) rather than raw formatValue, which is reasonable. Edge cases handled: a malformed hash, a missing record (catch block), a record with no drawable profile, and repeating groups/non-numeric values.
evidence.s2_fit: lib/render2d/compare.ts is a 33-line wrapper over the existing adaptMetallic/caseOuterProfile (lib/shapes2d) and viewportFor/fullSectionPath/fmt (lib/geom/svg), exported from render2d/index.ts. site/src/lib/compare.ts reuses GROUP_ORDER, orderedFields, toleranceFor, FIELD_LABELS, FIELD_UNITS, formatValue and displayNumber. The UI uses the site's Label, NativeSelect and ShadcnButton and the `@layer legacy` + `[data-ui=…]` styling pattern used by every route. The touched files are limited to what the route needs (App, router, metadata, nav active state, i18n).
evidence.s2_tests: lib/render2d/compare.test.ts checks that the paths equal fullSectionPath in a shared viewport, that the head faces and axis align, the length difference at scale, the viewBox bounds, and that shotshell and undrawable records are refused. site/src/lib/compare.test.ts checks row order and membership, exclusion of tolerances, angles, pressures and the chamber, metric/imperial values, B−A sign, float noise, and the caption unit. router.test.ts covers encoding, reload and malformed hashes. All follow the repo's vitest/fixtures setup (CARTRIDGES from lib/testing/fixtures). Not covered: the Compare with select/button and the SVG/table accessible names, though the repo has no component-test setup.
evidence.s3_fixes: Bug: compareRows (step3.patch 82-108) now merges symbols from both records, inserting B-only symbols after their predecessor, and leaves the missing cell and Difference as ''. Tests assert delta L {a:'0.1', b:'', difference:''} and R3 {a:'', b:'13.51'} in metric and imperial. The lede and empty-state texts were updated in EN and DE to match. Style: step 3 made no change. Compare.svelte from step 2 already sets `text-align: right` on th/td with only th:first-child/td.symbol left (Compare.svelte:148-152, the same pattern as GroupTable.svelte:231-245), so the request is met in code with no regression. However, neither the commit nor the changelog acknowledges or explains the second point.
evidence.cross_step: Step 2 added and step 3 amended a line under `## [Unreleased]` in CHANGELOG.md, as CONTRIBUTING requires. No version bump was made, which matches the stated strategy of bumping only in the `chore(release)` PR. Commits `feat(site): add a view comparing two cartridges` and `fix(site): list dimensions only one compared cartridge publishes` follow the convention and the 72-character title rule. All new code is in vitest's include paths and tsconfig's include (../lib/**/*.ts), and the exhaustive Record<Route['view']> in metadata.ts and Record<Page> in App.svelte were both extended, so the CI checks would plausibly pass.

unmet_requirements: Step 1 (review criterion): GitHub Actions are referenced by version tags (@v4/@v5/@v3), not pinned to full commit SHAs

Step 1 (review criterion): release.yml grants contents: write to the whole job, including npm ci/test/build, which is not least-privilege; pages.yml's workflow_dispatch has no main-only guard in the file
strengths: The compare feature reuses lib/shapes2d, lib/geom/svg and lib/core fully (caseOuterProfile, viewportFor, fullSectionPath, orderedFields, FIELD_LABELS, formatValue, displayNumber), so the new logic is two small modules

The release setup is coherent and enforced: the tag workflow checks that the tag is on main, matches package.json and the lock file, and has a changelog section; CONTRIBUTING gives a step-by-step process; Conventional Commits are stated and followed
The tests check concrete values against the data (B−A, metric/imperial, float noise, alignment and scale of the overlay, B-only rows after the step 3 fix)
issues: None of the workflow actions are pinned to commit SHAs (ci.yml, pages.yml, release.yml all use @vN tags)
release.yml gives contents: write to the job that also installs and runs third-party npm code; the publish step should be separated or permissions narrowed
Step 3's alignment point got no change and no explanation: the CSS already right-aligns (Compare.svelte:148-152), but the commit and changelog are silent on it
review.verdict: The repository setup, the compare view and the step 3 bug fix are careful, well-tested and consistent with the conventions step 1 introduced. Before merging, the actions should be pinned to SHAs and the release job's write permission narrowed. The response to the alignment comment, which needed no code change, should be stated explicitly.
